subject: He et al. (2020)
object: He et al. (2020) reported that a recurrent mutation in the TBPL2 gene caused diminished ovarian reserve and female infertility.

subject: Yang et al. (2021)
object: Yang et al. (2021) studied 2 unrelated families with female infertility caused by defects in oocyte maturation. The patients had repeated IVF failures, and only 2 immature metaphase I (MI) oocytes could be obtained from the patients.

subject: Yang et al. (2021)
object: In affected women from 2 unrelated families with oocyte maturation defects and infertility, Yang et al. (2021) used whole-exome sequencing with Sanger confirmation to identify a homozygous splice site variant in the TBPL2 gene (c.788+3A>G). Haplotype analysis showed that the disease alleles in the 2 families arose independently. A minigene assay showed that the variant disrupted the integrity of TBPL2 mRNA.

subject: Yang et al. (2021)
object: Yang et al. (2021) sequenced the transcriptome of affected oocytes carrying the TBPL2 variant and found that genes vital for oocyte maturation and fertilization were widely and markedly downregulated. They suggested that the mutation in the transcription factor TBPL2 led to global gene expression changes in oocytes.

subject: Wang et al. (2021)
object: Wang et al. (2021) described 2 infertile sisters from a consanguineous family who had female infertility caused by oocyte maturation arrest and degeneration.

subject: Wang et al. (2021)
object: Wang et al. (2021) used whole-exome sequencing to identify a homozygous missense mutation in the TBPL2 gene (c.895T>C, p.C299R) in 2 infertile sisters from a consanguineous family who had oocyte maturation arrest and degeneration. The authors described the mutation as rare and pathogenic. Functional studies showed that it impaired the transcription initiation function of the protein.

subject: Du et al. (2023)
object: Du et al. (2023) reported a 32-year-old woman who had unexplained primary infertility for 10 years. Most of her basal hormone levels were roughly normal, but her basal FSH was elevated. Her anti-Mullerian hormone level was normal. Two attempts at oocyte collection had failed, which was consistent with impaired ovarian folliculogenesis and failure of superovulation.

subject: Du et al. (2023)
object: Du et al. (2023) carried out whole-exome sequencing on the patient, then confirmed the result by Sanger sequencing in her family. They identified compound heterozygous TBPL2 variants: a novel nonsense variant, c.802C>T (p.Arg268Ter), and a previously reported variant, c.788+3A>G (reported as p.Arg233Ter). They checked allele frequencies in ExAC and gnomAD and assessed pathogenicity with SIFT, MutationTaster, and CADD. The authors concluded that these variants caused the impaired ovarian folliculogenesis, failed superovulation, and infertility.

subject: Ruotsalainen et al. (2024)
object: In a genomewide association study of 22,849 Finnish women with infertility and 198,989 control women who had given birth, from the FinnGen cohort, Ruotsalainen et al. (2024) used a recessive model and identified a genome-wide significant association with a stop-gained variant in TBPL2, rs144313315 (c.895A>T, p.Arg299Ter; NM_199047.3). The odds ratio was 650.1 (p = 4.11 x 10(-25)). The variant introduces a premature stop codon in the DNA-binding part of the protein, was predicted to cause loss of function with a CADD score of 40, and was associated only with infertility and no other diseases.

subject: Ruotsalainen et al. (2024)
object: Ruotsalainen et al. (2024) found that women homozygous for the TBPL2 p.Arg299Ter variant had significantly fewer offspring, an average of 0.16 compared with 1.75 in the other genotype groups (p = 1.4 x 10(-15)). Of 41 homozygous women, only 4 had given birth. All 4 had undergone IVF therapy; whether donor oocytes were used was not known. The authors concluded that the variant is associated with a rather severe form of infertility.

subject: Ruotsalainen et al. (2024)
object: Ruotsalainen et al. (2024) reported that the TBPL2 p.Arg299Ter variant has a minor allele frequency of 1.1% in Finland and is 43 times more frequent there than in non-Finnish Europeans. It is distributed fairly evenly across Finland, with regional allele frequencies of 0.84% to 2.38%. In gnomAD, loss-of-function variants in TBPL2 are rare, with this variant as the exception.

subject: Ruotsalainen et al. (2024)
object: Ruotsalainen et al. (2024) found that the TBPL2 locus acts recessively: the proportion of women with infertility was significantly higher only among those carrying two copies of the effect allele. The TBPL2 association was seen uniformly in both early-onset and late-onset infertility.

subject: OOCYTE/ZYGOTE/EMBRYO MATURATION ARREST 29
